newsitem.title: UK: ICI shares lose initial gain after results.
newsitem.headline: ICI shares lose initial gain after results.

text.p: Shares in Imperial Chemical Industries Plc lost an early advance by mid morning on Thursday, after results fell short of most expectations and sterling strength continued to overshadow profit prospects, dealers said.
The stock was down 3-1/2p at 761 by 0952 GMT in active trading of 3.6 million shares, after initially rising 15-1/2p.

Analysts at SBC Warburg upgraded the stock to a "buy" from "add" in the wake of the results but elsewhere traders said the results statement was unexciting and that prospects for the coming year remained mixed.
Dealers said ICI's plan to spin off its Tioxide unit was potentially positive, reducing the company's exposure to some of its most heavily cyclical operations.

Yet the continued strength in the pound, up sharply against the mark and dollar, threatened to squeeze ICI's export earnings. "The company has still got strong sterling to contend with," said another dealer.

ICI posted a drop in full year pre-tax pre-exceptional profit to 603 million stg from 951 million a year before. Analysts had expected yearly pre-tax pre-exceptional profits mostly in a range from 605 million stg to 650 million.

The past year had been a difficult one for the global chemical industry, ICI said, with "significant downward pressure on prices and margins," though paints had performed "exceptionally well" with profits up 60 percent.

It said the economic outlook for 1997 was better, with the major destocking that took place during 1996 believed to have come to an end, though the effects of higher oil prices, sterling strength and depressed chemical prices would continue to be felt in the first half of the current year.
